newsitem.title: USA: CSCE Dec coffee margins raised, back months cut.
newsitem.headline: CSCE Dec coffee margins raised, back months cut.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Wednesday it will raise trade margins for December 1996 coffee futures by $250, to $2,250, while margins on outer months positions will be lowered by an equal amount, to $1,750.
The change, which applies to exchange members or members of the trade, will take effect at the open of business October 10, the exchange said in a statement.

Meanwhile, margins on all straddle or arbitrage transactions involving the December 1996 contract will be raised by $500 to $1,200. The margin on all other "C" coffee straddle or arbitrage transactions will remain at $700, the exchange said.

The changes come just three weeks after an add-on "spot charge" of $1,000 for the nearby "C" contract was eliminated. At that time, the exchange said that with a decline in market volatility, the higher rates on the spot contract were no longer justified.
Margins for customers who are not members of the exchange or the trade will remain at a minimum of 140 percent above the required margins for the trade, the CSCE said.
The CSCE also said Wednesday it would adjust margin calls for straddle and arbitrage transactions on cocoa, sugar No. 11, cheddar cheese and dry milk futures.
For sugar No. 11 and for cocoa futures, minimum original margins for exchange members or members of the trade will be lowered by $50 to $150, for all straddle and arbitrage transactions.

For cheddar cheese and nofat dry milk, margins for all contract months will be reduced by $100 to $300. As a result, the exchange said, the inter-commodity straddle rate is decreased to $420 from $560 for cheddar cheese/nonfat dry milk, to $180 from $200 for cheddar cheese/milk and to $720 from $780 for nonfat dry milk.
The margin for all cheddar cheese and nonfat dry milk straddle and arbitrage transactions will be increased by $50, to $100.
Finally, margin rates for milk futures straddle and arbitrage transactions will be raised to $100, from $40.
All changes take effect on October 10. -- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
